dish: Kaisen-don (island seafood bowl) and Okinawan set meals
n: Shokuji-dokoro Nishikiya, Kouri Island (食事処 錦屋)
w: An Okinawan-cuisine and seafood-bowl canteen a short climb up from the Kouri Bridge landfall (look for the big shīsā), open 9:00–21:00; Okinawa Traveler profiles it and Mapple's Kouri Island drive guide lists it among the island's lunch stops.

dish: Motobu soba with flat, chewy wood-ash (mokkai) noodles
n: Sawanoya Motobu Honten (さわのや 本部本店)
address: Motobu-chō (Motobu Soba Kaidō, Prefectural Route 84), Kunigami-gun, Okinawa, Japan
w: One of the anchors of the 'Motobu Soba Kaidō' noodle road: noodles are hand-made the old way with wood-ash lye, giving firm, flat thick noodles with a distinctive flavour (Mapple); Stars and Stripes Okinawa features it in its guide to slurping noodles like a local.

dish: Okinawa soba in a bonito-forward dashi by a former French chef
n: Umi to Mugi to, Motobu (海と麦と)
w: Opened in Motobu in 2021 by a former French-cuisine chef whose bonito dashi has kept a queue outside ever since (OTV okitive); rurubu includes it in its 16 best Okinawa soba shops, traditional and new.

dish: Okinawa soba with soup poured from a kettle at the table
w: A 40-plus-year-old Nago soba shop known for topping up bowls with broth from a kettle (OCVB); voted into Okinawa Times' 2023 poll of 900 noodle fans for the best soba in the north.

n: Parlor Senri, Kin (パーラー千里) — CLOSED
w: The Kin parlor near the US base where founder Gibo Matsuzō created taco rice after opening in 1984; it closed on 29 June 2015 after 31 years (Ryukyu Shimpo). Its sister shop King Tacos, opened nearby, carries on the original recipe (rurubu).

dish: Shio-broth Okinawa soba with 3-day house noodles served 'kufa' (extra-firm)
w: Reopened in Yamada in April 2024 as the rebrand of a Tomari (Naha) soba shop that ran 8 years; noodles are rested 3+ days and ordered kufa (hard), regular or yafa (soft), in a clear pork-bonito-kelp shio broth with no pork bones (OTV okitive). OCVB's soba-lovers' picks feature it.
